title: How few real trials certify a robot policy when a biased simulator supplies the rest?
lede: research programme (proposal stage): valid, bias-agnostic sim-to-real evaluation of robot policies, consolidating about 130 twin projects into one question, with 13 checked references, hypotheses H1 to H6 and CoRL as the target venue
summary: An open research programme rather than a finished project. A digital twin is biased, so twin-only evaluation of a robot policy is wrong however many runs it makes; real trials are unbiased but scarce. The programme asks for estimators and tests that combine many twin runs with a few real ones, stay valid whatever the twin's bias, and say how many real trials they save, for mean return, failure rate and policy comparisons. It reconciles two answers already in this repository: control-variate savings that grow as 1/(1−ρ²) (twin-evaluation) and a worst-case result that a twin cannot shorten a failure-rate certificate (twin-certification). Planned: one estimator family under context pairing (control variate, PPI++, multifidelity Monte Carlo), a certification lower bound under checkable discrepancy assumptions, active choice of real trials, anytime-valid stopping, and tests on MuJoCo model pairs and on SIMPLER's published paired real and simulated results. No results yet: the proposal and log record the plan and the hypotheses before any experiment is run.
